trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the list's finishing line: it pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, with nothing extra to do. Everything on the list is single-player — no online, DLC or difficulty trophies — and PowerPyx's and KeenGamer's roadmaps put the full run at roughly 200 hours, most of it inside the 100% checklist behind A Long Road. Plan one long playthrough, keep rotating manual saves, and treat this trophy as a progress report rather than a task. Tip: if it does not pop when you expect, compare your earned list against the checklist here; the missing item is almost always a cleanup trophy from the middle stages of the roadmap.
trophies.unlock: Last of all: it pops automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is no separate task, mission or moment attached to it.
trophies.pitfalls: Chasing it directly wastes time. If it does not pop when expected, one cleanup trophy is still missing — audit your earned list against this checklist instead of replaying missions; there is no mission replay.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies on the list
Let the platinum pop automatically
If it stalls, audit the list for one missed cleanup trophy

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: This pops automatically at the end of Gone Fishing, the opening mission of Chapter 1, so it cannot be missed. Treat the mission as the game's tutorial stretch: movement, driving and the basics of the first protagonist's life. There is no performance requirement — no medal, timer or optional objective is attached. Tip: start your save discipline here and keep a manual save at the start of Chapter 1, because the game has no mission replay.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 1, at the end of Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the story.
trophies.pitfalls: Nothing about the trophy itself can go wrong. The time-waster is rushing on without starting manual-save discipline — keep a Chapter 1 save, because the balcony meditation window later in the chapter cannot be revisited.
steps: Start the story and play Chapter 1
Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing
Make a manual save at the chapter boundary

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing Chapter 1; it registers as you move into Chapter 2's opening mission. It is a pure progression trophy with no optional conditions, so a normal story run earns it. Optional missions you finish during the chapter still count toward the 100% checklist even before that checklist becomes visible. Tip: before closing the chapter, do Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house (see Positive Mental Attitude) — it is the one interaction the guides flag as potentially missable.
trophies.unlock: At the end of Chapter 1; the guides note it registers as you move into Chapter 2's opening mission.
trophies.pitfalls: Finishing Chapter 1 before doing Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house is the one costly mistake in this stretch — that interaction closes when the chapter ends (see Positive Mental Attitude).

Do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation before finishing
Cross into Chapter 2 to bank the trophy

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Completing Chapter 2 earns this; the guides note it registers during Chapter 3's opening stretch. Chapter 2 is also where both protagonists become playable together, which unlocks the partner trophies and, later, the final meditation spot. Nothing in the chapter is missable for trophy purposes. Tip: from here on, scan every new vehicle with the WAiNK app as you encounter it, so Whip It Good builds up naturally instead of becoming a late-game hunt.
trophies.unlock: At the end of Chapter 2; the guides note it registers during Chapter 3's opening stretch. Chapter 2 is also when both protagonists become playable together.
trophies.pitfalls: Nothing in the chapter is missable. The waste is reaching later chapters without the WAiNK scanning habit started — vehicle discoveries are slow and painful to backfill at the end of the run.
steps: Complete Chapter 2's main missions
Start Chapter 3 to trigger the unlock
Begin scanning new vehicles with the WAiNK app

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. The Cartel Heist sits inside this chapter and carries its own trophy (Break the Bank), so the chapter pays out twice. Progression is all that is required — no optional objectives or medals gate it. Keep doing optional missions as they appear: you need 100 of them across the game for the 100% checklist, and there are far more available than that. Tip: keep a manual save at the chapter's start and end and rotate the spare slots.
trophies.unlock: At the end of Chapter 3, the chapter that also contains The Cartel Heist (Break the Bank).
trophies.pitfalls: Skipping optional missions as they appear wastes progress that is expensive to reconstruct later — the 100% checklist needs 100 of them, and completions during the story already count.
steps: Complete Chapter 3's main missions, including The Cartel Heist
Move into Chapter 4 to bank the trophy
Keep a manual save at the chapter boundary

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the busiest chapter for named-mission trophies: Child's Play, Headliners and VCIA Takedown all live here. An optional Chapter 4 mission also opens up the bank vaults used by Maximum Withdrawal, so unlock them now rather than during cleanup. Everything in the chapter remains reachable afterwards in free roam. Tip: with the finale approaching, park one manual save at the chapter's end and do not overwrite it.
trophies.unlock: At the end of Chapter 4 — the chapter that also holds Child's Play, Headliners and VCIA Takedown.
trophies.pitfalls: Leaving the chapter without taking the optional mission that opens the bank vaults forces a later detour: Maximum Withdrawal depends on those vaults being open.

Take the optional mission that opens the bank vaults
Save at the chapter boundary

trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the final story mission. Once it is done the game returns you to free roam, so nothing after this point is locked away — the entire cleanup happens post-credits. There is no difficulty setting to worry about and no medal requirement on the mission itself. Tip: save before the finale in its own slot; with no mission replay, that save is your only way back to the ending stretch.
trophies.unlock: After the final story mission in Chapter 5; free roam continues afterwards, so the whole cleanup happens post-credits.
trophies.pitfalls: Overwriting your pre-finale save removes your only way back to the ending stretch — there is no mission replay. Keep the finale save in its own slot.

Complete it to roll the credits
Continue in free roam for the cleanup stages

trophies.name: Trust

No optional objectives or performance targets apply. Tip: story missions also move several background counters (discoveries, optional content), so there is no reason to rush past the areas it takes you through.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 2, on completing the mandatory story mission Breakfast Run.
trophies.pitfalls: None for the trophy — it is compulsory story progress. Rushing past the areas the mission visits only slows the background discovery counters that feed later trophies.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a set-piece story mission in Chapter 3; finishing it earns the trophy with no side conditions. It doubles as training for the free-roam robbery trophies: vault work, escapes and wanted-level management all return in Maximum Withdrawal and A Classic Blitz Play. Tip: pay attention to how the heist handles its escape phase — losing the heat quickly and switching vehicles is the same skill the silver robbery trophy grades you on.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 3, on completing The Cartel Heist and its escape.
trophies.pitfalls: Treating the heist as a one-off wastes its training value: its escape phase teaches the vehicle-switching and heat management that the free-roam robbery trophies grade you on later.

Complete the heist and its escape

trophies.guide: Complete Child's Play, a main mission the guides place in Chapter 4. Like the other named-mission trophies it is awarded for completion alone — no score, time or optional objective is attached. It sits in the chapter alongside Headliners and VCIA Takedown, so Chapter 4 banks several bronzes in a row. Tip: none; play it as it comes and keep your chapter-boundary saves current.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 4, on completing the main mission Child's Play.

It is the last of the named-mission bronzes and, like the rest, is awarded for completion alone on the compulsory story path. After it, only the finale stands between you and the gold for the final mission. Tip: keep a fresh manual save before pushing into the endgame sequence.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 5, on completing Operation Savage Glory — the last named-mission bronze before the finale.

Complete the mission

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The long gold. After the story, a 100% Completion checklist appears under Progress > Stats, and filling it earns this trophy — but '100%' is generous: Push Square's 100% checklist breakdown puts it near 60% true completion, with most side quests and many collectible types not required at all. The demanding parts are the categories required in full — robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests — plus 70 of the 80 challenges and any 100 optional missions (Push Square's checklist figures). Progress made during the story already counts, and the cited guides list nothing on the checklist as missable. Tip: work the checklist screen itself as your to-do list after the credits, and leave the hardest challenges for last, since you are allowed to skip ten.
trophies.unlock: Effectively post-story: the 100% Completion checklist appears under Progress > Stats once the story is done, although progress made during the story already counts toward it. Track it on this card: the checklist percentage, of 100.
trophies.pitfalls: Grinding categories the checklist only partially requires wastes hours — Push Square's checklist breakdown puts '100%' at roughly 60% true completion. Clear the fully-required categories first, use the checklist screen itself as the to-do list, and leave the hardest challenges for last: ten may be skipped.
steps: Finish the story to reveal the checklist
Open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion
Clear the fully-required categories first: robberies, ranges, drone races, Bret's quests
Reach 70 of 80 challenges and 100 optional missions
Top off the partial categories until the checklist reads 100%

sources.name: PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap · A Long Road

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete any 250 of the game's 397 stunt events. They fall into four families — 130 stunt jumps, 202 flights under bridges, 40 knife flights between buildings and 25 base jumps — and any mix counts toward the 250. The under-bridge flights are widely reported as the quickest to bank. Progress is tracked per region under Progress > Activities > Stunts, and completed stunts stay marked on the map's Exploration filter. Tip: the 100% checklist wants 300 stunts, so keep going past 250 while you are in a stunt mood.
trophies.unlock: Any time in free roam once stunt events are available; the counter runs to 250 of the game's 397 stunts, in any mix of the four families.
trophies.pitfalls: Stopping at 250 wastes momentum — the 100% checklist wants 300, so bank the extra 50 while routes are fresh. Repeating an already-completed stunt adds nothing to the counter.
steps: Open the map's Exploration filter to list stunt spots
Start with under-bridge flights for quick completions
Mix in jumps, knife flights and base jumps
Reach 250 completed stunts

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every kind of activity once. The trophy tracker counts nine activity types, and you can watch them under Touch Pad > Progress > Activities, where each type shows how many times you have done it. The story introduces most types on its own; the rest appear as blue icons once the map is unfogged. In practice this pops by itself during a full playthrough. Tip: late in the run, open the Activities page and look for any type still showing zero — that is your only homework.
trophies.unlock: Whenever the last of the nine activity types is tried for the first time; the story introduces most types, and the rest appear as blue icons once the map is unfogged. This card's tracker counts types tried, of 9.
trophies.pitfalls: Assuming it will pop on its own is the trap. Late in the run, open Progress > Activities and hunt any type still showing zero — that single missing type is the whole remaining task.
steps: Open Progress > Activities to see the nine types
Try each type at least once
Use the map's Activities filter to find any missing type

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge: 42 golds spread across 12 ranges, as the published lists and this bounty's own rules text both state. A gold is a score target rather than a win against an opponent, so learn each challenge's target pattern and retry until the medal lands; ranges stay available for the whole game. All 42 are also required in full by the 100% checklist (Push Square's 100% checklist breakdown), which makes this one of the list's true long poles. Tip: settle on one comfortable weapon per range and run its challenges back-to-back while the layouts are fresh in your mind.
trophies.unlock: Across the whole game: gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges, spread over the 12 ranges; ranges stay available from when you first reach them through the cleanup.
trophies.pitfalls: Switching weapons every attempt resets your learning curve — settle on one comfortable weapon per range and run its challenges back-to-back while layouts are fresh. Anything below gold does not count, and all 42 are also required in full by the 100% checklist (Push Square's breakdown).
steps: Visit each of the 12 shooting ranges
Learn each challenge's scoring targets
Retry until every challenge shows a gold medal — 42 in total

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. Only one win per location is needed for the trophy, even though each location hosts more races and the 100% checklist wants the remaining races at each location — so fly the shortest event at each spot and move on. Drone races are handling tests: a clean line through the gates beats raw speed. Tip: if a location's win is elusive, learn the gate order at cruising pace first, then push for pace on the next run.
trophies.unlock: In free roam: win one Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. This card's tracker counts locations won, of 14.
trophies.pitfalls: Winning extra races at a location you have already won adds nothing to this trophy — one win per location. Save the remaining races at each location for the 100% checklist.
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race location
Win one race there
Repeat at all 14 locations

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — winning the same race twice does not count. There are about 40 races in the game, so you can take the half that suits you and skip the rest. Wins count across race types, so mix road, off-road and water events as they appear on the map. Tip: keep track of which races you have already won; the map marks discovered races, and variety matters more than volume here.
trophies.unlock: Across the run: win 20 different races, from the roughly 40 races in the game, in any mix of road, off-road and water events.
trophies.pitfalls: Re-winning a favourite race does not advance the counter — only distinct wins count. Track which races are already won; variety matters more than volume.
steps: Enter races as they appear on the map
Win each race once
Reach 20 distinct race wins

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots, spread across 10 locations; most are ordinary free-roam visits, and doing a spot with both protagonists also feeds the 100% checklist (which itself only asks for 15 of the 18). The catch is the first one: in Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia announces a morning meditation at Jason's house and heads to the balcony — follow her and accept. That interaction disappears when Chapter 1 ends, and PowerPyx and GTABase both flag this as the list's only potentially missable trophy point; whether the trophy strictly needs it is unconfirmed, but the safe play costs two minutes. Tip: keep a Chapter 1 save untouched until the balcony meditation is done.
trophies.unlock: Across the game at all 18 meditation spots in 10 locations. One interaction is Chapter 1 only, per PowerPyx and GTABase: after Down to Earth, Lucia's morning balcony meditation at Jason's house, which becomes unavailable when Chapter 1 ends. If that balcony spot counts toward the 18, missing it would force a fresh playthrough; published sources do not resolve whether it counts, so the flag is a safe default. The final spot needs both protagonists playable together.
trophies.pitfalls: If that balcony spot counts toward the 18, letting Chapter 1 end before the balcony meditation would force a fresh playthrough — there is no mission replay — but published sources do not resolve whether it counts. Do the two-minute safe play anyway, and keep a Chapter 1 save untouched until it is done.
steps: In Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, talk to Lucia at Jason's house in the morning
Follow her to the balcony and accept the meditation
Visit the remaining meditation spots across Leonida — 18 in total
Do the final spot once both protagonists are playable together

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three Collectible Card sets. Cards are a collectible family scattered through the world and its interiors, and a set completes when every card in it has been found. Collectible types are only partially required by the 100% checklist, but this trophy wants three full sets, so aim your hunting at finishing sets rather than scattering single pickups across all of them. Tip: when you find a card, check which set it belongs to — completing the sets you are already closest to is far faster than starting every set at once.
trophies.unlock: When the third complete Collectible Card set is finished — a set completes when every card in it has been found.
trophies.pitfalls: Scattering single pickups across every set is the slow route. When you find a card, check its set, and finish the sets you are already closest to first.
steps: Pick up collectible cards as you explore
Track your progress set by set
Finish any 3 complete sets

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game app you also use to scan vehicles (it unlocks during Chapter 1), and its marked interaction points are spread across Leonida. Weave them into normal travel — one use per new neighbourhood adds up quickly over a 200-hour run. Tip: the map's Exploration filter lists discovered spots by name, which makes hunting down the last few far easier than driving around hoping to spot them.
trophies.unlock: From Chapter 1, when the WAiNK app unlocks; the counter runs to 100 marked locations across Leonida.
trophies.pitfalls: Saving WAiNK spots for a late-game hunt wastes hours — use the app once per new neighbourhood as you travel. For the last few, the map's Exploration filter lists discovered spots by name.

Use it at marked locations as you travel
Reach 100 WAiNK locations

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's 80 challenges. Challenges come in eight categories of ten — combat, vehicle and more — and are available from early on, with progress visible in the Progress menu. The 100% checklist raises the bar to 70, so treat 50 as a waypoint rather than the finish line. Tip: because you may ultimately skip the ten hardest challenges entirely, bank the easy categories first and save your frustration budget.
trophies.unlock: From early in the game, at 50 of the 80 challenges (eight categories of ten), with progress visible in the Progress menu.
trophies.pitfalls: Burning out on the hardest challenges is unnecessary — the 100% checklist raises the bar only to 70, so ten challenges can be skipped entirely. Bank the easy categories first and treat 50 as a waypoint, not the finish line.
steps: Open the challenge list in the Progress menu
Clear the easiest categories first
Reach 50 completed challenges — and 70 on the road to 100%

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, earn a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely. 'Partner' means the other protagonist — several trophies only open once Jason and Lucia are both playable, from Chapter 2 onward. Commit enough mayhem to reach four stars, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear; the guides point to covered spots such as train tunnels as reliable escape cover. Tip: stage it somewhere with a fast car and cover nearby, rather than improvising in the open.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 2 onward, once both protagonists are playable together: with your partner beside you, reach a 4-star wanted level and lose it completely.
trophies.pitfalls: Trying it solo, or letting the wanted level fall away before it reaches four stars, voids the attempt. Stage it near reliable cover — the guides point to train tunnels — with a fast car ready, rather than improvising in the open.
steps: Play with both protagonists together (Chapter 2 onward)
Raise the wanted level to 4 stars
Break pursuit and stay hidden until the level fully clears

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner, without your wanted level dropping in between. The chain is the hard part: finish one robbery, keep the heat alive, and start the next before the stars fade. Plan a small circuit of nearby shops in one district so travel time does not bleed the wanted level away. Tip: keep your partner with you for all three and use one fast car for the whole run.
trophies.unlock: Chapter 2 onward, with your partner: rob 3 shops back-to-back without the wanted level dropping in between. Track the current chain on this card: shops robbed back-to-back, of 3 — a current chain that resets if the wanted level drops, not a cumulative total.
trophies.pitfalls: Picking shops far apart bleeds the wanted level away during travel and breaks the chain — plan a tight circuit of nearby shops in one district, keep your partner with you for all three, and use one fast car for the whole run. The 3 is a current chain that resets if the wanted level drops — not a cumulative total.
steps: Group with your partner and pick 3 nearby shops
Rob the first shop and keep the wanted level up
Rob the second and third before the heat drops

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app (available from Chapter 1) registers it, and boats and aircraft count as well as cars. The 100% checklist wants 200 of the 277 base models scanned, so this trophy is the halfway mark of a habit worth starting on day one. Tip: scan everything parked or passing whenever you enter a new area — variety is everywhere early and genuinely painful to hunt down late.
trophies.unlock: From Chapter 1, when vehicle scanning with the WAiNK app unlocks; the counter runs to 100 discovered vehicles — boats and aircraft count as well as cars.
trophies.pitfalls: Starting the habit late turns variety into a hunt: scan everything parked or passing whenever you enter a new area. This trophy is only the halfway mark — the 100% checklist wants 200 of the 277 base models.
steps: Unlock vehicle scanning in Chapter 1
Scan every new vehicle, boat and aircraft you meet
Reach 100 discovered vehicles

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies during a single activation of Combat Focus, the slow-motion combat ability. You need a crowded fight: a gang operation or a robbery gone loud gives you the target density. Line up your targets before triggering Focus so all five takedowns fit inside one window. Tip: build your Focus stat through normal play beforehand so the window lasts as long as possible.
trophies.unlock: In any sufficiently crowded fight — a gang operation or a robbery gone loud: five takedowns inside a single Combat Focus activation.
trophies.pitfalls: Triggering Focus in a thin fight wastes the window. Line up at least five targets before activating, and build your Focus stat through normal play beforehand so the window lasts as long as possible.

Drop five enemies before the effect ends

Get into an aircraft on the field
Take off without any scheduled flight

roadmap.title: Roadmap to the Platinum — Vice Got a Price!
roadmap.intro: One playthrough, no difficulty settings and no online trophies: PowerPyx's and KeenGamer's roadmaps put the platinum at roughly 200 hours and a 4/10 difficulty. There is no mission replay, but free roam continues after the story, so almost everything can be cleaned up post-credits. Keep a manual save at the start and end of every chapter and rotate the spare slots, and never use cheats on a trophy run — they disable trophies and saving. Stage effort notes are estimates derived from each stage's composition, following PowerPyx's and KeenGamer's roadmaps. Estimates such as roughly 200 hours and 4/10 difficulty are from PowerPyx's and KeenGamer's published roadmaps — see Sources & methodology.

stages.name: Play the story — chapters and named missions
stages.rationale: The five chapters (PowerPyx's roadmap puts them at about 60–80 hours) award every story trophy automatically on completion, in list order from Gone Fishing to the final mission. Do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation during this stage: that spot belongs to Positive Mental Attitude, whose 18-spot counter is worked in stage 3, but the balcony itself must be done here, during stage 1 (see the missables note). Take optional missions as they appear, and scan vehicles and study animals as you travel — all of it counts toward later stages.
stages.warning: Chapter 1 window: Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house (Positive Mental Attitude) becomes unavailable when Chapter 1 ends, per PowerPyx and GTABase — do it before you finish the chapter. The balcony spot belongs to Positive Mental Attitude, whose 18-spot counter is worked in stage 3, but the balcony must be done during this stage. If that balcony spot counts toward the 18, missing it would force a fresh playthrough; published sources do not resolve whether it counts, so this is the safe default. A Long Road is never at risk from this one: its 100% checklist needs only 15 of the 18 spots.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: the bulk of the run — PowerPyx puts the five chapters at about 60–80 hours of the roughly 200-hour platinum. 12 trophies, all automatic on completion.

stages.name: Stranger strands and character quest lines
stages.rationale: Finish the six named character quest lines — Andy (Lucia), Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone (Jason), plus Bret's hunting line — and complete eight qualifying stranger strands for the Strangers & Freaks silver: six named character quest lines plus the Strangers & Freaks silver itself make this stage's 7 trophies. Trophy quest givers all return after the story, and PowerPyx and KeenGamer list no lockout in this stage.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: a medium stage — 7 trophies, all multi-mission strands rather than counters, so progress comes in whole missions at a time (estimate from PowerPyx's strand breakdowns).

stages.name: Collectibles and exploration
stages.rationale: The map-wide counters: all 18 meditation spots — the first of them was the Chapter 1 balcony handled in stage 1 — 3 full card sets, 100 WAiNK locations, 100 discovered vehicles and every area of Leonida explored. These reward steady habits during the story more than a dedicated grind at the end.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: small if built as habits during stage 1, large if left to the end — 5 trophies but four big counters (18 spots, 3 sets, 100 WAiNK uses, 100 vehicles) plus full map exploration.

stages.name: Activities, ranges and challenges
stages.rationale: 250 stunts, one try of each of the nine activity types, all 42 shooting-range golds, a drone-race win at all 14 locations, 20 race wins, Cal's fishing challenge, one arcade game and 50 challenges. The shooting ranges and drone races are required in full by the 100% checklist (Push Square's 100% checklist breakdown), so this stage is on the critical path.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: the skill-heavy stage — 8 trophies, dominated by the 42 shooting-range golds and 250 stunts; the ranges and drone races are required in full by the 100% checklist (Push Square's breakdown), so none of it is wasted (estimate from PowerPyx's guide).

stages.name: Free-roam feats and robberies
stages.rationale: The one-off moments and the robbery set: partner feats, five bank vaults, an armored truck, one illegal operation per gang, a stealth jewelry job, and the list's oddball world moments. Robberies are required in full by the 100% checklist (Push Square's 100% checklist breakdown) and generate the Marked Bills that stage 6 launders.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: the widest stage — 17 trophies, mostly one-off moments that take minutes each once set up, plus the robbery set; the long pole inside it is Actions Speak Louder's cumulative 500 choices, which fills across the whole run rather than in this stage alone.

stages.name: Money and property
stages.rationale: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills, spend $100,000 across shops, buy all eight garages and register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. These complete themselves if you launder after every robbery and buy property as areas open.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: the lightest stage — 4 trophies that complete themselves if stage 5's robberies are laundered as you go and garages are bought as areas open (estimate from PowerPyx's guide).

stages.name: 100% completion — A Long Road
stages.rationale: After the credits, work the checklist at Progress > Stats > 100% Completion: Push Square's 100% checklist breakdown puts it at roughly 60% true completion; it needs the fully-required categories plus 70 of 80 challenges and 100 optional missions (Push Square's checklist figures), and the cited guides list nothing missable on it.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: 1 trophy, but the list's biggest single time sink — KeenGamer's roadmap puts most of the roughly 200-hour run inside this checklist (see the rationale above for its share of true completion).

stages.name: The platinum — Vice Got a Price!
stages.rationale: With every other trophy earned — the story set, the strands, the counters, the activities and A Long Road — the platinum pops on its own; there is nothing extra to do. If it does not pop, one cleanup trophy is still missing: compare your earned list against the checklist.
stages.effort: Effort estimate: none — the platinum pops on its own once stages 1–7 are done.

missables.note: The full list was screened trophy by trophy against the official descriptions and the published guides (PowerPyx, GTABase, KeenGamer and GTA-Zone). Exactly one trophy is flagged — as a potential missable, below. No mission replay exists, but free roam continues after the story and every quest giver returns, so nothing else can be permanently missed.

items.name: Positive Mental Attitude
items.when: Locks when Chapter 1 ends: the Chapter 1 balcony meditation at Jason’s house becomes unavailable once Chapter 1 ends. In Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia announces a morning meditation at Jason’s house and goes to the balcony; follow her and accept before finishing the chapter.
items.detail: Why “potential”: the balcony meditation raises the meditation counter but is not marked as one of the 18 spots, so whether the trophy strictly requires it is unresolved in every published guide. The decision rule used here: if the balcony is one of the 18 marked spots, the trophy is missable; if it is not, it stays earnable in free roam. Since no source resolves it, the trophy is flagged as the safe default and the meditation is worth the two minutes. The 100% checklist separately needs only 15 of the 18 marked spots, so A Long Road is never at risk from this.
items.label: Potential missable

alsoGoodToKnow: There is no mission replay and no New Game+, so keep a manual save at the start and end of each chapter and rotate the spares.
Cheats disable trophies and saving — keep them off for the whole trophy run; they only unlock after the credits anyway.
Several optional missions and quest givers disappear or pause during the story, but the guides confirm none of them gate a trophy: every trophy quest giver returns, including after the story.
The 'Irredeemable' criminal profile is permanent once earned and makes police more aggressive, but PowerPyx confirms it does not block any trophy.

cleared.name: Actions Speak Louder
cleared.line: PlayStation tracks it as a cumulative counter to 500 choices, so no single choice can lock it — it fills up as you play.

platinumPlan.title: Platinum plan — the shape of the whole run
platinumPlan.composition: The list: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver and 46 bronze — 55 trophies, 28 of them hidden on PlayStation until earned. Everything is single-player: no online trophies and no difficulty trophies, so one playthrough on any settings earns the lot. Estimates such as roughly 200 hours and 4/10 difficulty are from PowerPyx's and KeenGamer's published roadmaps — see Sources & methodology.

phases.name: 1 · Story run
phases.detail: Play the five chapters start to finish (roadmap stage 1). Every story trophy is automatic; take optional missions as they appear and build the scanning, WAiNK and animal-study habits that feed the later counters.

phases.name: 2 · Chapter 1 missable window
phases.detail: Inside the story run, before Chapter 1 ends: after Down to Earth, follow Lucia to the balcony at Jason's house and accept the morning meditation — the Positive Mental Attitude window, per PowerPyx and GTABase. If that balcony spot counts toward the 18, missing it would force a fresh playthrough; sources do not resolve whether it counts, so do the two-minute safe play and keep a Chapter 1 save.

phases.name: 3 · Cumulative grinds
phases.detail: The counters that fill across the whole run rather than in one sitting: 500 choices (Actions Speak Louder), 250 stunts, 100 WAiNK locations, 100 discovered vehicles, $250,000 laundered and $100,000 spent. Weave them into travel and robberies instead of saving them for the end.

phases.name: 4 · Cleanup
phases.detail: Post-credits free roam: finish the strands, the one-off world moments and the robbery set, then work the 100% Completion checklist itself (Progress > Stats) until A Long Road lands — the fully-required categories first, the ten skippable challenges last.

phases.name: 5 · Platinum
phases.detail: With the other 54 earned, Vice Got a Price! pops on its own. If it does not, audit the checklist for one missed cleanup trophy.

longPoles: Actions Speak Louder — the cumulative counter to 500 choices; it fills across the whole run, so never skip conversations.
The Shootist — gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges across the 12 ranges, also required in full by the 100% checklist (Push Square's 100% checklist breakdown).
A Long Road — the 100% Completion checklist itself: Push Square's checklist breakdown puts it at roughly 60% true completion, and KeenGamer's roadmap puts most of the roughly 200-hour run inside it.

methodology.title: Sources & methodology
methodology.intro: Every guide on this page is written for this page, in our own words; the sources each guide rests on are linked beside it. The published guides used across the list:

guides.name: KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap
Push Square — GTA 6 Trophy Guide and Roadmap
GTA-Zone — GTA 6 Trophy List: All 55 Trophies and Achievements

notes: Trophy names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list (2026-11-18), reproduced verbatim and verified byte-identical against it — that verbatim text is labelled “Official description” on every card. The tracker data behind the official list comes via PSNProfiles and Exophase; both are cited by name only, because their GTA VI pages could not be verified, so no links are given for them.
The Shooting Range total of 42 challenges (The Shootist) follows the make.fun gta6-trophy-guide-01 competition rules text, which states it directly.
Missable flags were screened trophy by trophy against the official descriptions and the guides above; the reasoning is shown in the roadmap’s missable panel.

New in this edition: every trophy also carries a 'When it unlocks' line and a 'Pitfalls' line, both written from the official description and the same cited guides — where no published guide confirms a trigger (The Truth Is Out There, Ten Pin, Personal Best, Bad Luck, I Guess, Challenging Tank), the card says so and names the sources checked rather than inventing a method. Counters follow the targets PlayStation tracks or the totals stated in the cited guides (9 activity types, 14 drone-race locations, 52 areas, 9 gangs, 8 garages, the 100% checklist percentage).
